raw_response:
I've been farming this land for over thirty years. My father farmed it before me. Around here in Quzhou, everyone grows winter wheat then summer corn on the same fields — that's what this land is good for, that's what the government extension station supports, and that's what I know how to do well. I have about 10 mu of cropland.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October after the summer corn comes off. I'll buy the improved variety from the county seed shop — I stopped using saved seed years ago after a bad harvest. I'll plough before planting, put down compound fertilizer at planting, then spread urea at jointing in spring. I irrigate at overwintering, at jointing, and at heading — three times is what my father did and what I do. Rust and aphids have been bad some years lately, so I'll spray twice.

For summer corn, I plant right after the wheat comes off in June — I can't waste days. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now, yields are better. I just do rotary tillage, no time for a full plough. Corn doesn't need as much water here in summer because of rain, but I'll water once if it gets dry at silking. I spray once for corn borer.

I keep about 1 mu near the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, whatever the family needs. I don't count that in my main plan.
